Sorry, but not happy with this product.  In defense of this Dista filter, we have terrible tasting well water.  I'm not sure what exactly is in our water, but sediment builds up in the tank of our toilets and it leaves orangish brown staining in our shower.  That having been said, the Kenmore brand filter we used in our refrigerator prior to buying this product got our water tasting decent.  When I switched to this new filter, however, there was a drastically change in the taste of the water for the worse to the point that I actually put the old Kenmore filter (that was still draining in the sink) back in our fridge.  Even though the Kenmore filter is well overdue to be replaced, it is still yielding a far better taste than the brand new Dista filter.  When I went looking for a new filter for our fridge, I really only looked to see what would fit as I think about the different "levels" of filtering.  I'll need to read a little more closely next time as it looks like this one really only lessens the chlorine taste.  Too bad also that I paid for a twin pack, as the other one will remain unused!

We've been buying LG branded water filters for years. When we installed this water filter and ran water through it muddy water came out for a bit. We know we have to run the filter through for a bit to clear up any sediment, but this was about 1000x as much sediment as we have ever seen. Regardless, after a few quarts it started coming out clear. After many gallons of flushing later we tasted the water. It has that plastic taste. Again, the LG branded filters don't have this after-taste.

We immediately pulled out the filter and threw it away and ordered LG filters.

The filter is identical in outward appearance to the one sold under the GE brand. it fits exactly into the refrigerator. I haven't run a chemical analysis to determine if it has the same efficiency as the GE brand, but I would certainly feel safe in assuming so. The paper insert with the filter claims to have identical performance. And it's much, much cheaper than the GE brand. The filter is made in China. So, why not 5 stars? It's a small point, but the American flag on the box gives the implication that it's American-made. I believe it is there in an attempt to make the buyer believe it's American made. I don't think there's anything wrong with making products in China, nor do I find Chinese-made products defective. I think it's better to be open and up front with your customers - tell it like it is. Product is 5 stars, packaging is 3 stars, average is 4 stars.
